mainTopic: The מנורה's decorations, height, gold and heavenly design; then the rules of letters in a מזוזה
overview: The גמרא finishes counting the decorations of the מנורה: 22 גביעים, 11 כפתורים, and 9 פרחים, with the ninth flower coming from a פסוק in במדבר. רב says the מנורה is nine טפחים tall. When challenged from the three-step stone the כהן used, he explains that he meant only from the branches up. Next, 'מכלות זהב' is explained to mean that שלמה's ten מנורות used up all his pure gold, refined from a thousand כיכרים down to one each. The גמרא then asks why the מנורה is called 'טהורה.' Since a metal vessel can obviously become טמא, the word must teach that its design came from Heaven. This leads to teachings about fiery models shown to משה, גבריאל showing the מנורה, and things ה׳ pointed out with His finger. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה about the מזוזה: even one letter not surrounded by blank parchment makes it unfit. It then discusses a hole in the letter ה״י and begins a story about אגרא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The goblets and knobs add up correctly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes counting the 22 גביעים and shows how the פסוקים give exactly 11 כפתורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Add the eighteen goblets on the branches, and that makes twenty-two. The knobs also come to eleven: two on the main shaft, six on the branches, and the three knobs under the pairs of branches. That makes eleven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is checking the numbers of decorations on the מנורה against the פסוקים. The goblets come to 22 and the knobs come to 11, so both numbers work out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues a count that started before this section. The 18 goblets on the six branches are added to the ones on the main shaft to reach 22. For the knobs, the main shaft has two, each branch has one, and the פסוק adds three more 'and a knob' under the pairs of branches, which gives 11.

keyTerms.meaning: The branches of the מנורה
Knobs, the round decorations on the מנורה
Its own, meaning the ones on the main shaft itself
Here is, this makes (used when adding up a total)

phrases.english: and the eighteen of the branches,
this makes twenty-two.
The knobs too: eleven knobs:
two of its own, and six of the branches,
phrases.notes: 'Its own' means the main shaft in the middle of the מנורה.

phrases.english: and 'a knob,' and 'a knob,' and 'a knob,'
phrases.notes: שמות 25:35 says 'and a knob' three times, one under each pair of branches.

phrases.english: this makes eleven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַמְנֵי סְרֵי דְּקָנִים, הָא עֶשְׂרִין וְתַרְתֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the counting of the מנורה's decorations that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוקים give exactly 22 גביעים and 11 כפתורים.

steps.title: The flowers seem to come out only eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where nine פרחים come from, since the obvious count from the פסוקים gives only eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where do we get nine flowers from? There are two flowers on the main shaft and six on the branches. That is only eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same kind of count for the flowers, and this time it does not match. The teaching says nine, but the count only reaches eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the goblets and knobs, every item could be found in a פסוק. With the flowers, the same method finds two on the shaft and one on each of the six branches, so one flower is missing. The question is: which פסוק gives the ninth flower?

keyTerms.meaning: Flowers, the flower-shaped decorations on the מנורה
From where do we know this? (asking for a source)
Eight

phrases.english: But nine flowers, from where do we know this?
The flowers are two of its own,
and six of the branches —
that makes eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the goblets and knobs matched, the same counting method fails for the flowers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that the מנורה had nine פרחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting from the פסוקים gives 2 on the shaft plus 6 on the branches, which is only 8.

steps.title: A verse in במדבר gives the ninth flower
steps.stepSummary: רב שלמן points to the פסוק 'from its base to its flower', which shows an extra flower near the base of the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שלמן said: It is written, 'From its base to its flower, it is beaten work.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב שלמן answers the question by bringing a different פסוק, from ספר במדבר, that mentions another flower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in שמות only gave eight flowers. The פסוק in במדבר speaks of 'its flower' together with 'its base', so there was one more flower down by the base. That makes nine.

keyTerms.meaning: Its base, the bottom part of the מנורה
Beaten work, hammered out of one piece of gold

steps.whatToRemember: The מנורה had 22 גביעים, 11 כפתורים, and 9 פרחים. The ninth flower comes from the פסוק in במדבר, not from שמות.

phrases.english: Rav Shalman said:
It is written: "From its base to its flower,
phrases.notes: במדבר 8:4. The flower mentioned with the base is the extra, ninth flower.

phrases.english: it is beaten work."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the missing ninth flower.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an additional פסוק as a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the פסוקים in שמות count, so there are only eight flowers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק in במדבר adds a flower near the base, so there are nine.

steps.title: רב says the מנורה is nine handbreadths tall
steps.stepSummary: רב states that the height of the מנורה is nine טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The height of the מנורה is nine handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how tall the מנורה was. רב gives a measurement of nine טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the decorations. Now רב gives a size, and the next step will test whether this size makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Its height
The golden lamp in the משכן and בית המקדש
Handbreadths, a unit of measurement

phrases.english: Rav said:
The height of the Menorah is nine handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the count of decorations to a new subject: the height of the מנורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנורה is nine טפחים tall.

steps.title: Why would the כהן need steps for something so short?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא challenges רב from a משנה saying the כהן stood on a three-step stone to prepare the lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא challenged רב: There was a stone in front of the מנורה with three steps, and the כהן stood on it to prepare the lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא brings a משנה to argue against רב's measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine טפחים is lower than an average person's height. If the מנורה were that short, the כהן would not need to climb three steps to reach the lamps. So the משנה suggests the מנורה was much taller than רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: A stone
Steps
Prepares the lamps: cleaning them out and getting them ready for lighting

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Chiya challenged Rav:
There was a stone in front of the Menorah
and it had three steps,
on which the kohen stands
and prepares the lamps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's nine-טפחים measurement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the מנורה is nine טפחים tall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A three-step stone for the כהן means the lamps were too high to reach normally, so the מנורה must be taller than nine טפחים.

steps.title: רב meant only the part from the branches up
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the nine טפחים are measured only from where the קנים branch out, not from the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: שימי, are you the one asking this? When I said nine, I meant from the place where the branches start and upward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that his statement was not about the whole height of the מנורה. It was only about the upper part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's surprise ('Shimi, is it you?') shows he expected a scholar like רב שימי to understand. The nine טפחים measure only from where the branches come out to the top. The full מנורה, counting the part below the branches, is taller, so the כהן did need steps.

keyTerms.meaning: When I said it (explaining what he really meant)
The edge of the branches, the point where they come out of the main shaft
And upward

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not taking back his statement or saying the מנורה was short. He is clarifying that nine טפחים was only the top section, so there is no contradiction with the three steps.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's nine טפחים is measured from where the branches start and up, not the full height of the מנורה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Shimi, is it you (asking this)?
When I said it,
I meant from the edge of the branches and upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שִׁימִי אַתְּ? כִּי קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי's challenge by limiting what the measurement refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nine טפחים is the total height of the מנורה, so steps would not be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nine טפחים is measured only from the branches up. The full מנורה is taller, so the steps make sense.

steps.title: What does 'מכלות זהב' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the מנורה's parts and asks what the unusual phrase 'מכלות זהב' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסוק says the flowers, lamps and tongs were gold, 'מכלות זהב.' What does 'מכלות זהב' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a פסוק and asks about a strange word in it, setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מכלות' is not a normal word for gold. The גמרא wants to know what extra idea this unusual word is teaching about the מנורה's gold.

keyTerms.meaning: Flower, one of the decorations on the מנורה
Tongs used for tending the lamps
An unusual phrase describing the gold, explained in the next step

phrases.english: It is written: "And the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs,
of gold, and that 'michlot' gold."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 4:21.

phrases.english: What is meant by "michlot zahav"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the height of the מנורה to a new topic: the gold used to make it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the unusual word 'מכלות' in the פסוק.

steps.title: It used up all of שלמה's pure gold
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי explains that 'מכלות' comes from the word for 'used up': the מנורות used up all of שלמה's זהב סגור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי says: it means the מנורות used up all of שלמה's pure gold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי answers the question. He reads 'מכלות' as 'finishing off,' meaning the מנורות used up all of שלמה's finest gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He connects מכלות to the root כלה, which means to finish or use up. So the פסוק is telling us how much gold went into the מנורות, not just that they were gold.

keyTerms.meaning: That it used up or finished
Pure, top-quality gold

phrases.english: Rav Ami says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכִּילַּתּוּ לְכׇל זָהָב סָגוּר שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה,
phrases.english: That it used up all of Shlomo's pure gold.
phrases.notes: He hears מכלות as coming from the word for 'finishing off.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מכלות' means the מנורות used up all of שלמה's זהב סגור.

steps.title: A thousand כיכרים of gold for each מנורה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: שלמה made ten מנורות, each starting from a thousand כיכרים of gold, refined a thousand times down to one כיכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said: שלמה made ten מנורות. For each one he brought a thousand כיכרים of gold. They put it in the furnace a thousand times until it came down to one כיכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אמי by showing how much gold the מנורות really used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten מנורות times a thousand כיכרים is ten thousand כיכרים of gold, all refined down to just ten. That shows how the מנורות could use up all of שלמה's pure gold.

keyTerms.meaning: A talent of gold, a large unit of weight
Furnace for refining metal
They brought it down to exactly one כיכר

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda says that Rav said:
Shlomo made ten candelabrums,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אַחַת וְאַחַת הֵבִיא לָהּ אֶלֶף כִּכַּר זָהָב,
phrases.english: and for each and every one he brought a thousand talents of gold,
and they put it into the furnace a thousand times,
and brought it down to one talent.
phrases.notes: The תורה says the מנורה is made from a talent of pure gold (שמות 25:39).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אמי's explanation with a statement of רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב אמי's claim that the מנורות used up all of שלמה's pure gold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that each of ten מנורות was refined from a thousand כיכרים down to one.

steps.title: But שלמה had plenty of gold left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a פסוק says all of שלמה's drinking vessels and Lebanon-house vessels were gold, and silver counted for nothing. So his gold was not used up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? A פסוק says all of שלמה's drinking vessels were gold, the vessels of the Lebanon forest house were pure gold, and silver was worth nothing in his days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אמי. If the מנורות used up all of שלמה's gold, how did he still have so much gold for other vessels?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes huge amounts of gold in שלמה's palace, even 'זהב סגור.' That seems to contradict the idea that the מנורות finished off his gold.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A challenge to what was just said
Drinking vessels
שלמה's palace called the 'House of the Forest of Lebanon'

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְכׇל כְּלֵי מַשְׁקֵה הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה זָהָב
phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And all King Shlomo's drinking vessels were of gold,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל כְּלֵי בֵּית יַעַר הַלְּבָנוֹן זָהָב סָגוּר
phrases.english: and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כֶּסֶף נֶחְשָׁב בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה לִמְאוּמָה״!
phrases.english: silver was considered nothing in the days of Shlomo"!
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 9:20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אמי's reading that the מנורות used up all of שלמה's gold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows שלמה still had huge amounts of gold, so it could not all have been used up.

steps.title: Only the pure gold was used up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב אמי only meant שלמה's זהב סגור was used up, not all of his gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking only about the pure gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רב אמי's claim to one kind of gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אמי said 'כל זהב סגור,' not 'כל זהב.' So שלמה could still have had lots of ordinary gold for his other vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: We are saying, meaning that is what we meant

phrases.english: We are saying pure gold.
phrases.notes: He means only the finest gold was used up, not all of שלמה's gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the claim to a specific kind of gold.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אמי meant all of שלמה's gold was used up.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only שלמה's זהב סגור was used up. Other gold remained.

steps.title: Does refining really shrink gold so much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: a ברייתא tells that the מקדש's מנורה was only one dinar too heavy, and eighty rounds in the furnace removed only that dinar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does gold really shrink that much? A ברייתא says the מקדש's מנורה was one Kordikini gold dinar heavier than משה's. They put it in the furnace eighty times until it weighed exactly one כיכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's claim that a thousand כיכרים shrank down to one. A ברייתא shows that refining barely shrinks gold at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eighty rounds of refining removed only one small coin's weight, how could a thousand rounds remove 999 כיכרים? The two pictures of refining seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it really lose that much?
A type of gold coin, a very small weight compared to a כיכר
An incident that happened

phrases.english: And would it really be reduced that much?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
There was an incident where the Candelabrum of the Temple
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה בְּדִינַר זָהָב קוּרְדְיָקֵינִי,
phrases.english: was heavier than Moshe's by one Kordikini gold dinar,
and they put it into the furnace eighty times,
and brought it down to exactly one talent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, now aimed at רב's numbers in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that a thousand כיכרים were refined down to one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows eighty refinings removed only one dinar, so refining cannot shrink gold so much.

steps.title: Once gold is pure, it stops shrinking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: once the gold has been fully refined, it stays at that weight and barely shrinks anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once it is standing, it is standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the difference between raw gold and already-refined gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שלמה's time the gold was raw, so it lost a lot in the furnace. The later מנורה was already very pure, so eighty more rounds removed almost nothing. Both reports can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Once it is standing, it is standing. Once refined, it stays put

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'מכלות זהב' teaches that the מנורות used up all of שלמה's pure gold. Raw gold shrinks a lot in refining, but once pure it hardly shrinks.

phrases.english: Once it is standing, it is standing.
phrases.notes: Once the gold is fully refined, more time in the furnace barely changes its weight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two situations (raw gold vs. already-refined gold).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Refining always shrinks gold by about the same small amount, so רב's numbers seem impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Raw gold shrinks a lot; once it is pure, it barely shrinks.

steps.title: The design of the מנורה came from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that 'המנורה הטהורה' means its design came down from the 'place of purity,' from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: what does 'upon the pure מנורה' mean? That its making came down from the place of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רבי יונתן explains why the תורה calls the מנורה 'pure.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'טהורה' as describing where the מנורה's design came from: ה׳ showed משה how to make it. So the word teaches about its source, not about טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The pure מנורה, the phrase being explained
The place of purity, meaning Heaven
Its making, how it was to be built

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says that Rabbi Yonatan says:
What is meant by that which is written: "Upon the pure Candelabrum"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:4.

phrases.english: That its making came down from the place of purity.
phrases.notes: He means ה׳ showed משה how to build it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the word 'טהורה' describing the מנורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'המנורה הטהורה' teaches that the מנורה's design was shown from Heaven.

steps.title: Then the שלחן would also be from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the שלחן is also called 'טהור.' Would that also mean its design came from Heaven?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, 'upon the pure שלחן' would also mean its making came down from the pure place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבי יונתן's reading by applying it to the same word used for the שלחן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'טהור' appears for the שלחן. If 'pure' means 'designed in Heaven,' the שלחן would need the same meaning. The גמרא finds that unlikely, so the reading of 'pure' is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, introducing a problem with what was just said
The pure Table

phrases.english: But if so,
"upon the pure Table"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:6.

phrases.english: means that its making came down from the pure place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יונתן's reading from step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word is used for the שלחן, where 'designed in Heaven' does not fit, so the word must mean something else.

steps.title: 'Pure' means it can become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reading: calling the שלחן 'pure' implies it can become טמא, and the same is true for the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'pure' implies that it can become impure. Here too, the 'pure' מנורה implies that it can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first reading and explains 'טהור' in a way that works for both the שלחן and the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only call something 'pure' if it could also be 'impure.' So the word teaches that these כלים can become טמא. The same meaning fits both פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from which we learn
Ritually impure, here meaning it can become impure
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: This reading, that 'טהור' teaches the item can become טמא, holds for the שלחן. Steps 20-21 reject it for the מנורה and go back to רבי יונתן's reading.

phrases.english: Rather, "pure" implies that it can become impure,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי טְהוֹרָה – מִכְּלָל שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה.
phrases.english: here too, "pure" implies that it can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by replacing רבי יונתן's reading with one that fits both the שלחן and the מנורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'טהורה' means the מנורה's design came from Heaven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proposal is that 'טהור/טהורה' teaches the item can become טמא, for both the שלחן and the מנורה. Steps 17-21 accept this only for the שלחן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A proposal, not the final ruling: 'טהור' means the item can become טמא. It is kept for the שלחן but rejected for the מנורה in Steps 20-21.

steps.title: The word 'pure' really teaches something new about the Table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on Step 16. For the שלחן, 'טהור' is needed to teach that it can become טמא. Normally a wooden vessel made to stay in place cannot become טמא, but the שלחן was lifted to show the pilgrims the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense there, by the Table, as ריש לקיש explained. Why does the פסוק call it 'the pure Table,' which suggests it can become impure? It is a wooden vessel made to stay in one place, and such vessels cannot become impure! Rather, it teaches that they would lift it up to show the pilgrims the לחם הפנים, and say: 'See how much ה׳ loves you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins rejecting the answer from Step 16. It agrees that for the שלחן, 'pure' does teach that it can become טמא. This is the first half of an argument that will finish in Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By normal rules, the שלחן should not be able to become טמא at all: it is a wooden vessel made to rest in one place. So the word 'טהור' adds a real new idea: the שלחן was not always left in place, because it was lifted for the pilgrims. That makes it like a vessel that gets moved, and so it can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces a case that works, before showing one that does not)
By implication; from the fact that
A wooden vessel made to stay resting in one place (cannot become טמא)
Pilgrims who came up to the בית המקדש for the festivals
The special breads placed on the שלחן each שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the שלחן was never a fixed vessel. It still stood in its place. The lifting for the pilgrims is the special exception that lets it become טמא.

phrases.english: It makes sense there, as Reish Lakish explained,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the שלחן, the case from Step 16.

phrases.english: as Reish Lakish says:
What is the meaning of what is written: 'Upon the pure Table'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:6

phrases.english: Calling it pure implies it can become impure. But why?
It is a wooden vessel made to rest in one place,
and any wooden vessel made to rest in one place
cannot become impure!
Rather, it teaches that they would lift it up
for the festival pilgrims,
and show them the shewbread,
and the כהן would say to them:
See how beloved you are before the Omnipresent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts challenging Step 16 by showing that its reading fits the שלחן only because there it teaches something new.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that 'טהור' means 'can become טמא' works for the שלחן, but this sets up the claim that it does not work for the מנורה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For the שלחן, the inference is needed because a fixed wooden vessel normally cannot become טמא. That need will not exist for the מנורה.

steps.title: What 'affection' were the pilgrims shown?
steps.stepSummary: Stepping aside for a moment, the גמרא asks what the כהן meant by 'See your affection before ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'your affection' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a side question about the words the כהן said to the pilgrims. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just showing bread does not obviously show ה׳'s love. The גמרא wants to know what about the לחם הפנים showed that love.

keyTerms.meaning: Your belovedness; how dear you are
'The Place,' a name for ה׳

phrases.english: What is meant by 'your affection'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question on the last phrase of Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What about the לחם הפנים showed the pilgrims ה׳'s love?

steps.title: The miracle of the shewbread staying hot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a great miracle happened with the לחם הפנים: when it was taken off after a week, it was as fresh and hot as when it was put down.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי יהושע בן לוי said: a great miracle happened with the לחם הפנים. When it was removed, it was just like when it was set down, as the פסוק says: 'to put hot bread on the day it was taken away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question: the 'affection' was the miracle that the bread stayed hot and fresh the whole week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread sat on the שלחן for a full week, yet it came off as hot as when it went on. The proof is a פסוק that calls the bread 'hot' on the day it was removed. Showing this to the pilgrims proved ה׳'s love for them.

keyTerms.meaning: A great miracle
Its removal (taking it off the שלחן)
Its arrangement (setting it on the שלחן)
Hot

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the שלחן was lifted at all, which is the reason it can become טמא in Step 17.

phrases.english: It is like what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
A great miracle was done with the shewbread:
at its removal it was just like at its setting down,
phrases.notes: He means the bread was still fresh and hot after a whole week.

phrases.english: as it says: 'To put hot bread on the day it was taken away.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 21:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question from Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'affection' was the miracle that the לחם הפנים stayed hot and fresh all week, proven from a פסוק.

steps.title: For the מנורה, 'it can become impure' is obvious
steps.stepSummary: Back to the main point: for the מנורה, the word 'טהורה' cannot be teaching that it can become טמא, because metal vessels can always become טמא. There is nothing new to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, by the מנורה, does 'pure' mean it can become impure? That's obvious! It is a metal vessel, and metal vessels can become impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main argument and finishes rejecting Step 16's answer for the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed-in-place rule only protects wooden vessels. A metal vessel like the מנורה can become טמא anyway. So the פסוק would not need the word 'טהורה' to teach that, and Step 16's reading falls apart for the מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (by the מנורה)
It's obvious (so why would the פסוק need to teach it?)
Metal vessels
They are

phrases.english: But here, does 'pure'
imply that it can become impure?
That's obvious, they are metal vessels,
and metal vessels can become impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא, ״טְהוֹרָה״ מִכְּלָל שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה? פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main argument from Step 17 after the side discussion in Steps 18-19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects Step 16's reading only for the מנורה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A metal מנורה can obviously become טמא, so the word 'טהורה' would teach nothing new.

steps.title: So the מנורה's design came from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: Since 'can become טמא' does not work for the מנורה, the גמרא goes back to רבי יונתן's reading: 'טהורה' means its design came down from the place of purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that the way to make it came down from the place of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי יונתן's original explanation from Step 14 stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 had asked whether the שלחן being called 'טהור' would mean its design also came from Heaven. That question is now settled: for the שלחן, 'טהור' teaches about טומאה. For the מנורה, it teaches that its design came from Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Came down
Its making; how it was to be made
The place of purity (Heaven)

steps.whatToRemember: The same word 'טהור' teaches different things in different places. By the wooden שלחן, it teaches that it can become טמא. By the metal מנורה, that would be obvious, so it teaches that its design came from Heaven.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that its design came down from the place of purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from Step 20 and brings back רבי יונתן's reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'המנורה הטהורה' means the מנורה's design was shown from Heaven, as רבי יונתן said.

steps.title: Vessels of fire came down from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the idea: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says an ארון, a שלחן, and a מנורה made of fire came down from Heaven, and משה copied them, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that an Ark of fire, a Table of fire, and a מנורה of fire came down from Heaven. משה saw them and made the vessels just like them, as the פסוק says: 'See and make them like their pattern that you are being shown on the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the idea of vessels whose design came down from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה goes further than the מנורה alone. The ארון and שלחן also had heavenly models made of fire. The פסוק 'that you are being shown' tells us משה actually saw a model.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ark
Made of fire
Pattern; model
On the mountain (הר סיני)

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

phrases.aramaic: אָרוֹן שֶׁל אֵשׁ וְשֻׁלְחָן שֶׁל אֵשׁ
phrases.english: An Ark of fire and a Table of fire

phrases.aramaic: וּמְנוֹרָה שֶׁל אֵשׁ יָרְדוּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: and a Candelabrum of fire came down from Heaven,
and Moshe saw them and made the vessels like them,
as it says: 'And see and make them like their pattern'
phrases.notes: שמות 25:40

phrases.english: 'that you are being shown on the mountain.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of Step 21 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the design of the כלי המשכן came down from Heaven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, based on שמות 25:40.

steps.title: Was a fiery משכן also shown to משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if 'shown on the mountain' means a fiery model came down, then the same words about the משכן should mean a fiery משכן came down too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the פסוק 'And you shall set up the משכן according to its fashion which you were shown on the mountain', does that also mean a model was shown?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from step 22. Similar words are used about the whole משכן, so does that mean a fiery משכן came down too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the words 'shown on the mountain' were read as proof that fiery models came down. The same kind of words appear about the משכן. So the reading seems to prove too much, unless we can show the two פסוקים are different.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so. Used to show that an idea leads to a strange result.
Is it also so? Does the same apply here?
The Tabernacle, the portable Temple in the desert

phrases.english: But if that is so,
'And you shall set up the Mishkan according to its fashion
phrases.notes: שמות 26:30

phrases.english: which you were shown on the mountain,'
is that also so?
phrases.notes: He means: did a fiery משכן come down from Heaven too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading used in the ברייתא of step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'shown on the mountain' means an actual fiery model came down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same kind of wording is used for the משכן, so the reading would wrongly mean a fiery משכן came down too

steps.title: The wording is different: fashion versus pattern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משכן פסוק says 'according to its fashion', but the vessels' פסוק says 'after their pattern'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'according to its fashion'. There it says 'after their pattern'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to different words in the two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כמשפטו' means following the rules and instructions, so no model was needed for the משכן. 'כתבניתם' means a pattern or model, so an actual fiery model of the ארון, שלחן, and מנורה was shown.

keyTerms.meaning: According to its fashion, following its rules or instructions
After their pattern, following their model
Here / there. Used to compare two cases.

steps.whatToRemember: Only the ארון, שלחן, and מנורה were shown as a fiery model, because the פסוק says 'pattern'. For the משכן, משה only got instructions.

phrases.english: Here it is written 'according to its fashion,'
there it is written 'after their pattern.'
phrases.notes: 'There' is the פסוק about the vessels from step 22 (שמות 25:40).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the wording of two פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same idea of a fiery model should apply to the משכן
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כמשפטו' means instructions only, while 'כתבניתם' means a real model was shown

steps.title: גבריאל showed משה how to make the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that גבריאל, dressed like a worker, showed משה how the מנורה is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: גבריאל was wearing a kind of work belt, and he showed משה how to make the מנורה, as it says 'And this is the work of the מנורה'.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא is talking about the מנורה being shown to משה, it brings a related teaching: the angel גבריאל showed משה how to make it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'this' (וזה) in the פסוק suggests something was pointed at and shown. גבריאל wore a work belt like a craftsman, as if he were demonstrating the actual work.

keyTerms.meaning: A wide belt, like the kind a worker wears
Girded, wearing a belt
The way the מנורה is made

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Gavriel was wearing a kind of belt,
and he showed Moshe how the menorah is made,
as it is written: 'And this is the work of the menorah.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 8:4. The word 'this' hints that something was actually shown.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching about the מנורה being shown to משה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבריאל, dressed as a worker, showed משה how to make the מנורה, learned from the word 'וזה'

steps.title: Things God showed משה with His finger
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that three things were hard for משה until God pointed to them: the מנורה, the new moon, and שרצים. Some add the laws of שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: three things were hard for משה until ה׳ showed him with His finger: the מנורה, ראש חודש, and שרצים. Each one is learned from a פסוק that says 'this'. Some say the laws of שחיטה too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching in the same spirit. It lists the things God had to point out to משה, each learned from the word 'this' in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק uses 'זה' (this), which suggests pointing at something. A second opinion (יש אומרים) adds the laws of שחיטה to the list, based on the same kind of word in another פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: With His finger, pointing it out
The new moon, the start of the month
Small creeping creatures that are טמא
The laws of slaughtering an animal

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'זה' (this) in a פסוק is read as a sign that ה׳ pointed at the thing itself: the מנורה, the new moon, the שרצים, and according to some, שחיטה.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הָיוּ קָשִׁין לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: Three things were difficult for Moshe,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ,
phrases.english: until the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed him with His finger,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: מְנוֹרָה, וְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ, וּשְׁרָצִים.
phrases.english: and these are they: the menorah, the new moon, and creeping creatures.
The menorah, as it is written: 'And this is the work of the menorah.'

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ – דִּכְתִיב: ״הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים״,
phrases.english: The new moon, as it is written: 'This month shall be for you the beginning of months.'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:2

phrases.english: Creeping creatures, as it is written: 'And this is what is impure for you.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:29

phrases.english: And some say: also the laws of slaughtering,
as it is said: 'And this is what you shall do on the altar.'
phrases.notes: שמות 29:38

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the idea of step 25 to a list of things shown to משה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנורה, the new moon, and שרצים (and according to some, שחיטה) were shown to משה with God's finger, learned from the word 'זה'

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the two sections of the מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the two sections of the מזוזה hold each other back, and even one missing letter holds them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two sections in the מזוזה hold each other back, and even one letter holds them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of the מנורה and goes back to quote the next line of the משנה about the מזוזה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says both sections (שמע and והיה אם שמוע) are needed: without one, the other does not work. It adds that even one missing letter makes the מזוזה not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Sections of the תורה
The scroll placed on the doorpost
Hold back, prevent the מצוה from being done without them
Writing, here meaning a single letter

steps.confusionAlert: 'מעכבות זו את זו' does not mean one section causes harm to the other. It means you need both: without one, the other alone does not do the מצוה.

phrases.english: The two sections that are in the mezuzah
hold each other back,
and even one letter holds them back.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁבַּמְּזוּזָה מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sections of the מזוזה are needed, and even one missing letter makes it not kosher

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that one letter holds back the מזוזה, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers to teach something so obvious. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that every letter must be there seems simple, because the writing of a מזוזה must be complete. So the גמרא wants to know what new thing the משנה is teaching with the words 'even one letter'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Asks why something needed to be said at all.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the last clause of the משנה quoted in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'even one letter holds them back'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is plain that a missing letter ruins the writing, so the משנה seems to teach nothing new

steps.title: The rule is needed for the tiny tip of a יוד
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, answers that the משנה's rule teaches that even the small tip of a יוד holds back the מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The משנה only needed to say this to teach about the small tip of the letter יוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the question of why the משנה needed to say that one letter holds back the מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving out a whole letter is obviously a problem. So רב says the משנה must be teaching something smaller: even the tiny tip at the edge of a יוד counts, and if it is missing, the מזוזה is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... (this phrase explains why a ruling that seems obvious had to be said)
The small 'thorn', the little stroke at the tip of the letter יוד

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It was needed only
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's line that even one letter holds back the מזוזה.

phrases.english: for the thorn of a yod.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the rule is about a tiny part of a letter, not a whole letter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule about one letter seemed to state the obvious
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that even the tip of a יוד holds back the מזוזה

steps.title: But that is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: missing the tip of a יוד is also obvious, so a better answer is needed. Step 31 gives it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is also obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first answer, because a יוד without its tip is clearly not a proper letter either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tip is missing, the letter is not shaped correctly, so of course it is a problem. The answer did not show anything new that the משנה had to teach, so we need a better answer.

keyTerms.meaning: But this too...
It is obvious

phrases.english: But this is also obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that the rule teaches about the tip of a יוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A letter missing its tip is not properly formed, so this is just as obvious as a missing letter

steps.title: Every letter must have blank parchment all around it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's rule matches another teaching of רב: a letter not surrounded by blank parchment on all four sides is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is needed for another teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Any letter that does not have blank parchment around it on all four sides is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the משנה is teaching about a letter that is complete but touches another letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A letter that touches the letter next to it looks whole, so you might think it is fine. רב teaches that each letter needs blank space all around it. The משנה's 'even one letter' tells us that even one letter like this makes the whole מזוזה unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: For the other one (another teaching)
Parchment; here, the blank parchment around a letter
Surrounded
Four sides (above, below, right, left)
Unfit, not valid

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that 'even one letter holds it back' teaches רב's rule: every letter must stand alone with blank parchment on all four sides.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a missing letter. The letter is fully written. The problem is that its ink touches another letter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for writing סת״ם: letters that touch each other can make a מזוזה, תפילין, or ספר תורה unfit.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לִכְאִידַּךְ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rather, it is for the other teaching that Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Any letter that does not have parchment
surrounding it on its four sides –
is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לִכְאִידַּךְ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after Step 30 rejected the first one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a different case the rule covers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule was about the tip of a יוד, which is obvious
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule teaches that a letter not surrounded by blank parchment holds back the מזוזה

steps.title: A hole in the letter ה״י
steps.stepSummary: אשיאן בר נדבך, quoting רב יהודה, rules that a hole inside the ה״י is fine, but a hole in its leg makes it unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אשיאן בר נדבך said in the name of רב יהודה: If a hole was made inside the letter ה״י, it is fit. If the hole is in its leg, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a letter that got a hole in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the empty space inside the ה״י does not damage the letter itself. A hole in the leg damages the letter's shape, so this version says it is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: It got a hole, was punctured
Its inside
Its leg (literally, its thigh)
Fit, valid

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַשְׁיָאן בַּר נַדְבָּךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Ashiyan bar Nadbakh said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
If the inside of a heh got a hole, it is fit;
if its leg did, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַשְׁיָאן בַּר נַדְבָּךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new related topic: damage to a letter's shape
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole inside a ה״י is fit; a hole in its leg is unfit

steps.title: A second version: it depends how much of the leg is left
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי יעקב report a different version: a hole in the leg is fine if a piece the size of a small letter is still left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: רב הונא explained it to me himself. And רבי יעקב said: רב יהודה explained it to me himself. If a hole was made inside the ה״י, it is fit. If it was in the leg: if the leg still has the size of a small letter left, it is fit, and if not, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: Two sages report, each from his own teacher, a different and more detailed version of the ruling about a hole in the ה״י.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that a hole inside the letter is fine. They differ about the leg. The first version says any hole there makes it unfit. This version says it is still fit if the part of the leg still attached is at least as big as a small letter.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
Was left over, remained
The size of a small letter
And if not

steps.whatToRemember: A hole inside a ה״י is fine according to everyone. A hole in the leg depends on how much of the leg is left still attached.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁה לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: It was explained to me personally by Rav Huna,
and Rabbi Ya'akov said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁה לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: It was explained to me personally by Rav Yehuda:
If the inside of a heh got a hole, it is fit;
if its leg did – if there remains in it
phrases.notes: He means the part of the leg still attached to the roof of the ה״י.

phrases.english: the size of a small letter, it is fit,
and if not – it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁה לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, more detailed version of the ruling in Step 32
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole in the leg of a ה״י is fit if the attached part is at least the size of a small letter; otherwise unfit
